answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen price despite an 18% cost mandate, making renewal untenable. Memory_c2 shows that switching to a low-cost vendor delivered sharp unit cost cuts with quick onboarding and reliable invoicing—directly applicable to the current financial pressure. Memory_c4 demonstrates that benchmarking can move incumbents on price, but that path is already blocked. The assembly line runs at 94% capacity with no buffer, so any switch carries execution risk; however, a standard_experiment scale (partial volume or limited duration) with the low-cost vendor from memory_c2 would test their capability under current constraints while preserving the option to dual-source (memory_c3) if execution falters. This avoids deferral (which sacrifices the 18% target) and renewal (which violates the cost mandate). Verifying memory_c2 and memory_c4 will confirm whether the prior low-cost vendor relationship is still viable and whether price renegotiation is genuinely closed.
